For d,e>=q-1, a q-round EF game preserves a span isometry for first q-1 moves: before the last, t<=q-2 and a prescribed pairing fiber contains a vector beyond span; at last, with t<=q-1, 2^(q-1)>q possible responses allow preserving equality/adjacency even if linear dependence changes. For d<e, Spoiler chooses d+1 distinct independent isotropic x_i in S_e, which forces a nontrivial linear relation among pairwise orthogonal y_i in S_d; a final incompatible pairing functional exists on independent x_i, so Spoiler wins at move d+2. When d=1 the graph is K_3, detected by a nonedge at rank 2; all d>=2 contain both edges and nonedges. Induced claw in S_3 vs its absence in S_2 was independently enumerated; unrestricted proof is linear-algebraic.
